headline: 4% of global oil supply at risk as Saudi pipeline shuts down
summary: A critical East-West pipeline failure could stop 4 million barrels of daily exports, threatening to spike fuel prices and global inflation.
details: A critical Saudi Arabian oil pipeline has shut down, potentially cutting off approximately 4 million barrels of oil per day from the global market. This represents about 4% of the total global oil supply, according to reports from Reuters.

The pipeline is essential for transporting oil from the Arabian Peninsula to the Yanbu port on the Red Sea, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. Without it, Saudi Arabia's export reserves at Yanbu may only last five to seven days.

Industry sources suggest repairs could take anywhere from a few weeks to six weeks. While some believe limited supply can bet continued during repairs, the Saudi government and Ministry of Energy have not yet officially commented.
The International Energy Agency (IEA) reports that Saudi oil supplies have already hit a 30-year low in August due to decreased transport through the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz.

Adding to the crisis, Houthi rebels in Yemen have reportedly seized an island at the entrance of the Red Sea and have threatened to attack Saudi oil tankers, further complicating the transport of energy resources.

topic: ACC probes Asif Mahmud over corruption allegations
headline_marked: Asif Mahmud [[denies Bs 11,000 crore money laundering]] allegations by ACC
headline: Asif Mahmud denies Bs 11,000 crore money laundering allegations by ACC
summary: The NCP spokesperson claims the Anti-Corruption Commission is being used as a 'political tool' due to a lack of necessary reforms.
details: National Citizens' Committee (NCP) spokesperson Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan has directly denied allegations by the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) regarding the laundering of Bs 11,000 crore to countries including Australia, Dubai, and Singapore.
Speaking at a press conference in Banglamotor, Dhaka, Mahmud claimed that the ACC continues to be used as a political tool because essential reforms have not yet been implemented.

During the event, he criticized the current government's economic policies and employment initiatives, stating that while they promised 1 crore jobs for youth, they instead created opportunities for 50 lakh people from their own party through extortion.
Mahmud also expressed concern over the public processions of the banned Awami League, calling it a threat to the security of people's lives and property.
He further criticized the BNP for failing to take visible or effective measures to prevent the activities and anarchic processions of the banned organization.
NCP Chief Coordinator Nasir Uddin Patwari announced that the NCP will contest the upcoming local government elections independently.
Patwari warned that the 11 parties of the Jugapata Andolon will collectively resist any attempt by 'dark forces' to occupy centers or commit irregularities during the elections.
caption:
Asif Mahmud denies laundering Bs 11,000 crore to Australia, Dubai, and Singapore, calling the ACC a 'political tool'.

National Citizens' Committee (NCP) spokesperson Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan has directly denied allegations by the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) regarding the laundering of Bs 11,000 crore to countries including Australia, Dubai, and Singapore.

Speaking at a press conference in Banglamotor, Dhaka, Mahmud claimed that the ACC continues to be used as a political tool because essential reforms have not yet been implemented.

During the event, he criticized the current government's economic policies and employment initiatives, stating that while they promised 1 crore jobs for youth, they instead created opportunities for 50 lakh people from their own party through extortion.

Mahmud also expressed concern over the public processions of the banned Awami League, calling it a threat to the security of people's lives and property.

He further criticized the BNP for failing to take visible or effective measures to prevent the activities and anarchic processions of the banned organization.

NCP Chief Coordinator Nasir Uddin Patwari announced that the NCP will contest the upcoming local government elections independently.

Patwari warned that the 11 parties of the Jugapata Andolon will collectively resist any attempt by 'dark forces' to occupy centers or commit irregularities during the elections.
